title: Pinata Swing
summary: A party skill game: a decorated paper or clay pot hangs from a cord and is kept swinging while a player, eyes covered and turned around a few times, swings a stick at it. Each turn is short, and a clean hit on the middle of the pot is worth the most.
howToPlay: Press and hold to wind up the stick; the crosshair wanders because you cannot see well and have been turned around.
Release when the crosshair sits on the swinging pot; the stick needs a moment to arrive.
Three swings make a turn, and there are three turns.
rules: A hit on the middle of the pot scores 3, on the body of the pot 2 and on its edge 1; a miss scores nothing.
The pot swings from side to side and bobs up and down, and every turn starts you facing a slightly different way.
Stars are given for the total over all nine swings.
heritageNote: Hitting a hanging pot with a stick is a children's party game enjoyed in Mexico, Paraguay and many other countries of the Americas. The pot is made of paper or clay, decorated by hand, and the fun is in the swinging and the guessing.
